editorial:
You follow Wesley, a nervous twelve-year-old, on his first Boy Scout camping trip where he hopes to fix a friendship by chasing the mysterious Order of the Arrow. The camp feels alive with silly rules, loud counselors, and kids trying way too hard to look brave. Wesley’s awkward energy keeps the story warm, and his best friend’s hurt feelings give the jokes real heart. Instead of mean humor, the movie leans into goofy mistakes, embarrassing moments, and the kind of camp chaos that makes you laugh and wince at the same time.

The young cast sells every awkward beat, and the pacing rarely slows down once the secret-society hunt begins. Some jokes repeat and a few adult characters feel too cartoonish, but the emotional payoff lands. If you enjoy family-friendly comedy with campfire nostalgia, this is an easy pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Wesley discovers the Order is less a secret club and more a group of kids who help each other. He stops chasing status and finally talks honestly with his best friend. The twist is that the friend already wanted to forgive him, but needed Wesley to show up without a plan. They reunite at the campfire, and Wesley earns a simple badge that means more than any secret title.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves camp comedies and family-friendly adventures.
